Qiskit Fall Fest 2026.about: The Qiskit Fall Fest is a global series of events held at universities worldwide on the theme of quantum computing. Taking place annually, these events are primarily planned and run by students with support from IBM Quantum.

speakers.name: Matthieu Fortin-Deschênes
speakers.role: Head of Quantum Solutions / Product Owner
speakers.bio: Matthieu Fortin-Deschênes holds a PhD in engineering physics from Polytechnique Montréal and completed a postdoctoral fellowship in electrical engineering at Yale University. His research experience spans the development of new materials, both experimentally and computationally. He joined PINQ2 in 2023 as a product owner, where he develops and integrates quantum algorithms and hybrid algorithms for chemistry, materials science and computer-assisted materials discovery.

speakers.name: Brian Ingmanson
speakers.role: Engagement Lead, Quantum Innovation Centers in America
speakers.bio:
Brian Ingmanson is the Engagement Lead for Quantum Innovation Centers in America. He works with partners, educators, and students around the world to discover novel research and build skills in the field of quantum computing. He joined IBM in 2019 and helped to create global programs like the Qiskit Global Summer School and Qiskit Fall Fest. His accomplishments have earned him the IBM Outstanding Technical Achievement Award.

Previously Brian was a middle school science teacher, working at The Gilbert School in Winsted, CT for 6 years. He holds a B.S. and M.A. in Education from the University of Connecticut. Brian frequently presents on stage, and sometimes, plays the drums. Occasionally he’s known to do both at the same time.

speakers.name: Mohammad El Mir
speakers.bio: Mohammad El Mir is a Master’s student in École de Technologie Supérieure (ÉTS) under the supervision of Claude Crépeau. His thesis work is about quantum identification in the context of a satellite: With only a small, re-usable key, how is Alice capable of identifying Bob and vice-versa?

speakers.name: Denise Koch
speakers.bio: Denise Koch has over 20 years experience in the field of Advanced Research Computing (ARC) and joined the team of ARC Analysts at Concordia University in 2021, and has been specializing in quantum computing since 2023. Previously, Denise worked for 13 years as a Research Professional at the Centre for Research in Molecular Modeling (CERMM). She obtained a PhD in computational and theoretical chemistry from Concordia University in 2006, and then pursued a postdoctoral fellowship with James T. Hynes in molecular modeling at l’École normale supérieure, France.
